instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

items.t: Your cover runs from 1 November 2026 to 31 October 2027. Get each member's card made with Aadhaar e-KYC on beneficiary.nha.gov.in, the Ayushman app or at a CSC.
At an empanelled hospital, go to the Ayushman Mitra desk with the card. Treatment up to Rs 5 lakh a year is cashless, so do not pay cash for a covered treatment.
1800-180-2036 (Ayushman Bharat Haryana toll-free) / 14555 (Ayushman Bharat national helpline)
Haryana Parivar Pehchan Authority, Citizen Resources Information Department (CRID), Haryana

An 8-digit Family ID for every family living in Haryana, holding each member's details, income and bank account in one record. Almost every Haryana scheme uses it, from pensions and ration cards to Chirayu health cover and Lado Lakshmi, so once it is verified you need not prove the same things again. Making or updating it is free. You can create it yourself online, or get it made at a CSC, Saral Kendra or PPP operator.
Free Family ID that opens Haryana schemes and selects you for benefits automatically
Every family living in Haryana should enrol. It gets a permanent 8-digit Family ID
A family living outside Haryana that needs a Haryana service gets a 9-digit temporary ID starting with T
Creating, updating and downloading the Family ID are free, even at an operator. Never pay a fee
Income, caste and other details are verified by the department. Verified details cannot be edited later
Births, deaths and marriages are linked to it, so the record updates itself
Mobile number of the head of family, for OTP
Bank passbook of the head of family and earning members
Income details of every earning member (salary, farming, business)
Caste certificate, if you belong to SC, BC or another category
Disability certificate, if any member is Divyang
Parivar Pehchan Patra (Mera Parivar portal)
Do you Know Parivar Pehchan Patra (Family ID)?
Choose NO to make a new Family ID. Choose YES if your family already has one and you want to see or update it.
Aadhaar of the head of family. The system first checks whether you are already in some Family ID.
Sent to the mobile number linked with that Aadhaar.
Head of family: name, date of birth, gender
This number gets every OTP for the Family ID later, so give one you will keep.
Address (district, block or town, village or ward, house no.)
Choose General, SC, BC-A or BC-B. It is checked against your caste certificate.
Give true income. Schemes like Chirayu and Lado Lakshmi use the verified family income.
Bank account and IFSC (head of family)
Pensions and other scheme money are sent to the account recorded here.
Add everyone who lives and eats together. Married daughters go to their husband's Family ID.
Open meraparivar.haryana.gov.in and choose I want to create my PPP, or open the PPP citizen login page and answer NO.
Search with the head of family's Aadhaar and verify the OTP. Then fill in the head's details, address, caste, income and bank account, and add each member with Aadhaar.
Submit and note the acknowledgement number. If the portal asks, download the filled PPP form, have the head of family sign it and upload it. After this, only one change is allowed.
The department verifies income and other details through records and field checks. Checked details are marked Verified.
The 8-digit Family ID comes by SMS. Download it any time on meraparivar.haryana.gov.in with the Family ID and an OTP.
If you cannot do it yourself, a CSC, Antyodaya Saral Kendra or PPP operator does it free. For wrong income or caste, use the correction module or Report Grievance on the PPP site.
0172-4880500 (Family ID helpline, 9 am to 6 pm, Monday to Saturday) / 98886 33322 (PPP helpline)
Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana (Lado Lakshmi)
SEWA Department (Social Justice, Empowerment, Welfare of SCs & BCs and Antyodaya), Haryana

Rs 2,100 a month for women aged 23 and above from the poorest families of Haryana. From the second month, Rs 1,100 comes to your savings account and Rs 1,000 is saved for you in a government recurring deposit, paid back with interest when it matures (within five years). You apply only on the official Lado Lakshmi mobile app using your Family ID (PPP). There is no paper form, and any other link or form is fake.
Rs 2,100 a month (Rs 1,100 in hand + Rs 1,000 saved in a government RD)
Woman aged 23 or above. Any number of eligible women in one family can apply
Family income verified in the Family ID (PPP) not more than Rs 1 lakh a year, and the family endorsed as poorest of the poor by the Gram Sabha or Ward Committee

Or family income up to Rs 1.80 lakh if a child in a government school scored over 80% in Class 10 or 12, reached the NIPUN grade level in Classes 1 to 4, or was brought out of malnutrition (SAM/MAM). Mothers of more than three children cannot use this route
She, or her husband if she married into Haryana from another state, has lived in Haryana for at least 15 years
Not for women already getting the old age, widow, Divyang or Ladli allowance or any other government pension, government employees whose family income is above the limit, or income tax payers
Family ID (Parivar Pehchan Patra) with verified income
Aadhaar card of the applicant, and Aadhaar details of family members
Savings bank account in the woman's own name
Vehicle ownership details and HKRN ID, if any
A smartphone, with the mobile number for OTP and the monthly face check
Type your number in the app and enter the OTP. The eligibility and payment SMS come here.
The 8-digit Family ID. Your income and family details are taken from it.
The app shows the members on the Family ID. Pick the woman who is applying. She must be 23 or older.
If you married into Haryana from another state, your husband's 15 years of residence counts.
Give any car or other vehicle owned by the family. It is checked against transport records.
Only if you or a family member work through Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam.
Must be in the woman's own name. PFMS checks it before the first payment.
Asked by SMS after verification. If you choose Rs 1,500 or less, Rs 500 is paid and Rs 1,000 still goes into the RD.
Install the Lado Lakshmi app (made by HARTRON for the Haryana government) from Google Play or the App Store. Do not use any other app, link or form.
Register with your mobile number and OTP, choose Apply for the Scheme, enter the Family ID and pick the woman who is applying.
Fill in the Aadhaar, residence, electricity, vehicle and bank details and submit. Note the Registration ID shown on screen.
CRID checks your details against Family ID records within 15 days. If you are eligible, an SMS asks you to choose the monthly amount: confirm it and give consent in the app with your Registration ID.

The District Social Welfare Officer creates your DDLLY ID and PFMS checks the bank account. Payment starts the next month: Rs 2,100 in full the first month, then Rs 1,100 to the account and Rs 1,000 to the RD.
After the first payment, do the face check (Blink to Click) in the app every month, or the money stops. Raise any complaint in the app's grievance window: the DSWO must act within 7 days.
1800-180-2231 (toll-free Lado Lakshmi helpline) / 0172-4880500 (Family ID and verification helpline)
Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh-Samman Nidhi Yojana (Rs 1,500 for Women)
Department of Social Justice & Empowerment (Directorate of Empowerment of SCs, OBCs, Minorities & Specially Abled), Government of Himachal Pradesh

Rs 1,500 a month for women of Himachal Pradesh from families with an income below Rs 2 lakh a year and no government job or pension. It began in 2023 in Lahaul-Spiti as the Indira Gandhi Mahila Samman Nidhi. In 2026 the rules were tightened: the income limit came in April, so earlier applications had to be made again, and from June the age is 21 to 59. Only one woman per family is paid and BPL families come first. You apply on a free form at the Tehsil Welfare Officer's office, and payments are being started area by area after verification.
A woman who is a permanent (bonafide) resident of Himachal Pradesh, aged 21 to 59
Family income below Rs 2 lakh a year; BPL families get priority
Only one woman in a family can get the money

Not eligible if anyone in the family is a regular, contract, outsourced or daily-wage government employee or a pensioner, a serving or retired soldier or a soldier's widow, or works for a panchayat, urban body, board or corporation
Not eligible if anyone in the family is an Anganwadi worker or helper, ASHA, mid-day meal or multi-task worker, gets a social security pension, pays income tax or is registered for GST
Buddhist nuns (chomo) living permanently in a monastery in Himachal are also eligible
Proof of age (birth certificate, school certificate or Aadhaar)
Family income certificate showing income below Rs 2 lakh
Copy of the bank passbook with IFSC
Ration card (towns) or copy of the Parivar Register (villages)
Buddhist nuns: a certificate from the chief chomo of the monastery

Collect the application form free of cost from the Tehsil Welfare Officer's office in your tehsil (or the District Welfare Officer's office), fill it, attach the documents and hand it in at the same office. Take your income and bonafide certificates along; they can be made at a Lok Mitra Kendra on HimSeva first. Incomplete forms are returned within 15 days for correction. Since June 2026 the forms go to the Tehsil Welfare Officer, not to the panchayat.
The woman's own name, as on Aadhaar and the bank passbook.
As written in the Parivar Register or ration card.
You must be at least 21 and not over 59. Attach the age proof.
Village Dhalli, Panchayat Bhatta, Tehsil Theog, District Shimla
Village, panchayat, tehsil and district where you live permanently.
Income of the whole family from all sources, as in the income certificate. It must be below Rs 2 lakh.
Tick Yes only if the family is on the BPL list; BPL women are taken first.
An account in your own name; the Rs 1,500 is paid here every month.
Villages give the Parivar Register copy, towns give the ration card.
You declare that no one in the family is a government employee, pensioner, ASHA or Anganwadi worker or in the other excluded groups, and that no other woman of the family gets this money.
Get your bonafide Himachali certificate and an income certificate (below Rs 2 lakh) from a Lok Mitra Kendra or the tehsil.
Collect the free form at the Tehsil Welfare Officer's office.
Fill it, attach the documents, and hand it in at the same office. Ask for a receipt.
The Tehsil Welfare Officer checks the form and documents and sends the list of eligible women for approval.
Once approved, Rs 1,500 is paid into your bank account every month. Payments are being started area by area, so ask the welfare office when your area's turn comes.
Block and district officials verify the application. Once approved, Rs.2,500 arrives in your Aadhaar-linked account by the 15th of every month.
When the Anganwadi worker or block office calls you for satyapan or e-KYC, complete it. Names that are not verified do not get the next instalment.
If the money stops, check at the bank that the account is still linked to Aadhaar, then call 1800-890-0215 or complain at the block office.
1800-890-0215 — toll-free, Department of Women, Child Development & Social Security, Jharkhand
Directorate of Social Welfare, Department of Women, Child Development & Social Security, Government of Jharkhand

Money for girls in Jharkhand to stay in school and not be married off early: Rs.2,500 in Class 8, Rs.2,500 in Class 9, Rs.5,000 each in Classes 10, 11 and 12, and a one-time Rs.20,000 at age 18 to 19, Rs.40,000 in all. It goes to the first two daughters of a mother who study in government or government-aided schools. For school girls the school applies, by sending the girl's details from e-Vidya Vahini to the scheme portal. Others apply with the official form at the CDPO office.
Girls living in Jharkhand, enrolled in Class 8 to 12 in a government, government-aided, welfare-department or NCLP school
Only the first two daughters of a mother; the mother gives a self-declaration
Parents must not be permanent or retired central or state government or PSU employees, or draw a government pension or family pension
Parents must not pay income tax
For the Rs.20,000 grant she must be 18 or 19 years old when applying, and a voter ID is needed
Aadhaar card of the mother (of the father, if the mother has died)
Bank or post office passbook in the girl's name
Mother's self-declaration on birth order, and the parents' self-declaration that they are not taxpayers or government employees
Principal's certificate that she studies in the school; for orphans, the parents' death certificate and a Child Welfare Committee certificate
Savitribai Phule Kishori Samriddhi Yojana portal

Girls in Class 8 to 12: ask the headmaster or class teacher. The school sends the girl's details from e-Vidya Vahini to the Savitribai portal, adds her Aadhaar, bank account and declarations, and forwards it to the CDPO. Girls of 18 to 19 who have left school, and anyone the school has not covered: fill the official form and hand it in at the Child Development Project Officer (CDPO) office of your block, yourself or through your Anganwadi worker. Attach self-attested copies of the ration card, Aadhaar, voter ID and bank passbook, the self-declarations and the principal's certificate. Girls still in school at 18 to 19 can apply through the school.
As on her Aadhaar and school register.
The mother's name comes first. A guardian is written only for an orphan.
Barwadih, Barwadih panchayat, Chas block, Bokaro district
In a town, write the nagar nigam, nagar panchayat or nagar parishad instead of the block.
Only if you know it. The Anganwadi worker can tell you.
जन्म तिथि / जन्म प्रमाण पत्र संख्या (Date of birth / birth certificate number)
Attach a copy of the birth certificate. For the 18–19 grant, also give the voter ID number.
Only the first or second daughter can apply. The mother signs a declaration on this.
The girl's own 12-digit Aadhaar number.
बैंक/पोस्ट ऑफिस खाता संख्या, शाखा, IFSC (Bank or post office account, branch, IFSC)
An account in the girl's own name. The money is sent here by DBT.
Govt. High School Barwadih, Class 9, Roll 27
The principal signs a certificate that she studies in this class.
Tick the one class she is in now, or 18–19 years for the Rs.20,000 grant.

At the start of the school year, tell the class teacher that she wants the Savitribai benefit, and give copies of her Aadhaar, the mother's Aadhaar, the birth certificate, the bank passbook and the ration card.
The school sends her details from e-Vidya Vahini to the Savitribai portal, adds the Aadhaar, bank account and declarations, and forwards the application to the CDPO.

For the Rs.20,000 grant at 18 or 19 after leaving school, fill the official form, attach the self-declarations and voter ID, and submit it at the CDPO office or through the Anganwadi worker. Keep the receipt.
The CDPO checks the application and the District Social Welfare Officer approves it. Wrong details are sent back to the school for correction.
The money for that class comes by DBT into the girl's account. Check the status on savitribaipksy.jharkhand.gov.in under Track Beneficiary Status.
Repeat every year from Class 8 to Class 12, then apply for the Rs.20,000 grant at age 18 or 19.
0651-2400757 / 0651-2223544 — Directorate of Social Welfare, Ranchi (technical help, savitribaihelpdesk@gmail.com) / 1800-890-0215 — department toll-free
Ayushman Bharat – Arogya Karnataka (AB-ArK Health Card)
Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Karnataka — Suvarna Arogya Suraksha Trust (SAST)

Karnataka's health cover, run together with the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. Families with a BPL (Priority Household or Antyodaya) ration card get free treatment up to Rs.5 lakh a year for the whole family; other families get 30% of the treatment cost paid, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year. Treatment starts at a government hospital, which refers you to a listed private hospital if it cannot treat you; listed emergencies can go straight to a listed hospital. The card is made at a government hospital counter for Rs.10 with your Aadhaar and ration card.
BPL families: up to Rs.5 lakh a year free; other families: 30% of the cost, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year
Every resident of Karnataka with an Aadhaar card can enrol
Eligible category (free treatment up to Rs.5 lakh per family per year): families with a Priority Household (BPL) or Antyodaya ration card under the Food Security Act
General category (APL card or no ration card): the government pays 30% of the package rate, up to Rs.1.5 lakh per family per year, and the family pays the rest
Simpler treatments are given only in government hospitals. A private hospital needs a referral from a government hospital, except for the listed emergencies
Aadhaar authentication is compulsory before a referral to a private hospital
Aadhaar card of the patient (each member of the family enrols separately)
Ration card, which decides whether you are in the eligible or the general category
Mobile number, for the SMS with your ArK ID
Rs.10 for the card (Rs.20 for a reprint if it is lost)
Referral letter from the government hospital, when going to a private hospital
Earlier prescriptions, test reports and discharge papers, if any

At the registration (Arogya Mitra) counter of any government hospital: Primary Health Centre, Community Health Centre, taluk or district hospital, or medical college hospital. Take every member's Aadhaar card and the ration card, and Rs.10 per card. Grama One, Karnataka One and Bangalore One centres also issue the card.
The patient's own Aadhaar. Each family member is enrolled one by one.
Fingerprint on the biometric device. If it fails, the staff can use an OTP to the Aadhaar mobile or the QR code on the Aadhaar card.
From the ration card. It links you to your family in the food department's records.
Filled automatically: Priority Household or Antyodaya card = Eligible; APL card or no card = General.
Taken from the Aadhaar e-KYC. Check the spelling before the card is printed.
Signed — no other health insurance scheme
A printed form: you allow your Aadhaar to be used for enrolment and state that you are not covered by another scheme.
Your ration card number, a dash and your member number. It is printed on the card.
Paid once. A reprint of a lost card costs Rs.20.
Go to the registration counter of a government hospital (PHC, CHC, taluk or district hospital) with your Aadhaar and ration card.
The staff check your Aadhaar by fingerprint (or OTP or QR code), and your ration card decides your category: Eligible (BPL) or General.
Sign the consent and self-declaration, pay Rs.10, and collect the printed card with your ArK ID. Repeat this for each family member.
When you fall ill, go first to a government hospital. If it cannot give the treatment, ask the doctor for a referral to a private hospital empanelled under AB-ArK.
At the private hospital, go to the Arogya Mitra desk with the card, your Aadhaar and the referral letter. The hospital takes approval from SAST; for eligible families the treatment is cashless.
In an emergency covered by the listed emergency procedures, go straight to the nearest empanelled hospital. No referral is needed.
If a hospital asks a BPL card holder to pay for a covered treatment, call 104 or 1800 425 8330 before paying.
104 — Arogya Sahayavani (toll free); 1800 425 8330 — Arogya Karnataka helpline
Karnataka Social Security Pensions (Old Age, Sandhya Suraksha, Widow and Disability Pension)
Directorate of Social Security and Pensions, Revenue Department, Government of Karnataka

Karnataka pays a monthly pension to poor elderly people, widows and people with disabilities, straight into a bank or post office account. The old age pension is Rs.600 a month from 60 to 64 and Rs.1,200 from 65; Sandhya Suraksha gives Rs.1,200 to farmers, labourers, weavers and fishermen aged 65 and above; widows get Rs.800; people with disabilities get Rs.800 to Rs.2,000. One common form covers all of them, and you hand it in at the Atalji Janasnehi Kendra (Nadakacheri) for your area.
Rs.600 to Rs.2,000 a month depending on the pension; Rs.1,200 for most people aged 65 and above
Resident of Karnataka, with a family income below Rs.32,000 a year
